as_read: Weakly positive: one small trial of rosehip extract meets rule 2 on abdominal fat area (25834460); the osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis evidence is seed and shell powder at 5 g/day, manufacturer supported in the meta-analysis, and one 120-person powder trial had no between-group difference.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: abdominal fat area and body fat percent at 12 weeks
studies_to_add.quote: Abdominal fat area and body fat percent were measured as primary outcomes.

stop_list: Labels print rosehip fruit extract 500 mg without marker content, so 25834460's 100 mg/day extract can't be compared with them.
The three vitamin C labels print rose hips at 7.5 to 20 mg with an immune claim; no immune trial surfaced in the search and the amount is far below any studied dose.
stored_rating_note: Stored material_form and evidence are seed and shell powder at 5 g/day, which no label prints. Stored positive_moderate looks high: 18407528 says all three trials were manufacturer supported and the data sparse, and 41599942 reports no between-group difference in a 120-person powder trial. positive_weak fits better.
